A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Gaussian Splashing, despite the changed title. Their text, equations, tables and figures are readable, including v2's supplementary material. Content moved from v1's main text can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 5, Table 1 and the demonstration figures report original solid-fluid simulations, rendering ablations and runtime measurements.

after.justification: Section 5, Table 1 and supplementary Section 11 report original simulations, runtime measurements and visual comparisons, including new shadow, coastal-wave and rigid-contact results.

M1.justification: V1 uses shared solid particles with fixed Gaussian centers and volume regularization. V2 separates simulation particles from rendering Gaussians, transfers motion through GMLS, trains Gaussian positions and omits volume regularization from its stated loss, although Figure 2 still shows it. V2 also adds dynamic shadows and foam, spray and bubble rendering.

E1.justification: V2 adds coastal waves with foam, headset droplets, externally manipulated ficus and multiple colliding rigid bulldozers, substantially extending the demonstrated environments and interactions. V1's books-to-pool scene disappears. The separate LEGO-wave scenario and existing chair, garden, cup/dog, can and astronaut scenarios remain.

E2.justification: V2 adds a no-shadow rendering control against the shadow-enabled pipeline in Figure 6. Existing anisotropy, diffuse-only and inpainting controls remain, as does the density-grid-versus-NeuS sampling comparison, moved from v1 Figure 3 to v2 Figure 11.

E3.justification: Table 1 changes the reported Tension measurement from surface-particle detection to surface-tension constraint projection and reports maximum fluid counts instead of ranges. Cup & dog's maximum changes from 170K to 160K. Hardware, the 0.005-second timestep and 10/50 fluid/solid iterations remain unchanged; these disclosures do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: V2 adds the shadow-map ablation in Figure 6, testing how shadows affect depth and visual realism. The existing anisotropy, specular, inpainting and sampling analyses remain. Moving sampling figures and adding demonstration scenes does not constitute additional ablation evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Both present runtime point values without experimental uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V2 adds visual and timing results for Waves, Headset, Ficus and Bulldozers, plus timings for the retained LEGO-wave scenario. Book & Lego results and reconstruction/training-time entries disappear. Garden's reported simulation time changes from 10.3 to 7.3 seconds; changed methods and measurement definitions limit direct performance comparisons.

T1.justification: The supplement adds explicit cubic SPH kernel, gradient and angular-occlusion formulas; the volume-regularizer definition is removed from the text. Most existing constraints and Jacobians are retained or relocated, with no new proof. The new spring example in Section 7.1 inconsistently equates compliance with stiffness after defining compliance as inverse stiffness.

C1.justification: Despite the broader title and demonstrations, v1 already claims unified rendering and simulation of deformable solids, rigid bodies and fluids, including two-way coupling and object-state conversion. V2 retains the abstract's feasibility claim and the main contribution and novelty claims.

C2.justification: V2 explains the conflict between particle distributions suited to simulation and rendering, motivates decoupling, and adds interpretations concerning shadows and PhysGaussian's baked lighting. It broadens the refraction limitation to light transport generally, while dropping v1's warning that large fluid-particle counts impair rendering efficiency.

D1.justification: Sections 7–10 add substantial reproducibility detail: XPBD pseudocode, an 18-by-36 surface-detection representation, GMLS neighborhood transfer, shadow-map resolution and depth-dependent foam kernels. Existing simulator settings are relocated rather than changed. Reconstruction and training times are removed, and the printed project-page address changes without establishing any change in resource availability.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting GMLS, variance shadow maps and foam/spray/bubble techniques, alongside ClimateNeRF and GaussianAvatars. It adds targeted contrasts with PhysGaussian concerning coupled representations and baked lighting. The related-work categories and most existing research positioning remain.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the method explanation, places training before solid simulation/interpolation, and divides experiments into Ablation and Evaluation. Derivations, implementation settings and many demonstrations move into a structured supplement. The title, author presentation and citation style also change.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the teaser with a four-scene overview, redraws the rendering decomposition to include foam, and adds shadow and new-scene figures. Table 1 becomes a compact, grouped, single-column display with different columns. Numerous existing figures move into the supplement, alongside extensive typography and layout changes.

improvement.justification: The new shadow ablation and broader demonstrations strengthen support for the existing versatility claims, while the interpolation and rendering details aid reproducibility. These gains are tempered by removed reconstruction/training-cost reporting and new inconsistencies: Figure 2 retains a loss term omitted from the revised training equation, and Section 7.1 contradicts its own compliance definition. The net quality improvement is useful but limited.
